info.name: Looper AI — Financial Analytics Dashboard
info.description:
Complete API collection for the Looper AI Full-Stack Financial Analytics Dashboard assignment.

**How to use:**
1. Import this file into Postman.
2. Set the `baseUrl` collection variable to `http://localhost:5000` (already set).
3. Run **Auth / Login** first — the test script automatically saves the JWT to `{{authToken}}`.
4. All protected requests use `{{authToken}}` via Bearer token auth.

**Demo credentials:** admin@penta.com / password123

JWT token. Automatically populated after running the Login request.

item.name: Dashboard
item.description:
Analytics endpoints that return aggregated financial data calculated live from MongoDB.

All endpoints require Bearer `{{authToken}}`.

request.description:
**GET /api/dashboard/summary**

Returns aggregated financial summary calculated live from the transactions collection.

**Authentication required:** Yes

**Calculated fields:**
- `totalRevenue` — sum of all transactions where `category = "Revenue"`
- `totalExpenses` — sum of all transactions where `category = "Expense"`
- `balance` — `totalRevenue − totalExpenses`
- `savings` — same as balance (net income)
- `revenueChange` — month-over-month % change in revenue
- `expensesChange` — month-over-month % change in expenses
- `balanceChange` — month-over-month % change in balance
- `savingsChange` — month-over-month % change in savings

**Success 200:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "totalRevenue": 175432.50,
    "totalExpenses": 121850.75,
    "balance": 53581.75,
    "savings": 53581.75,
    "revenueChange": 12.5,
    "expensesChange": -3.2,
    "balanceChange": 8.1,
    "savingsChange": 8.1
  }
}
```

query.description: Calendar year to aggregate. Defaults to the most recent year in the dataset (2024). Integer.

request.description:
**GET /api/dashboard/trends**

Returns monthly revenue and expense totals for a full calendar year. Always returns 12 data points (one per month), including months with zero transactions.

**Authentication required:** Yes

**Query parameters:**
- `year` (integer, optional) — defaults to the most recent year in the dataset (2024)

**Success 200:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": [
    { "month": "Jan", "monthNum": 1, "year": 2024, "revenue": 18200.00, "expenses": 9450.50 },
    { "month": "Feb", "monthNum": 2, "year": 2024, "revenue": 14300.00, "expenses": 11200.75 },
    ...
    { "month": "Dec", "monthNum": 12, "year": 2024, "revenue": 12100.00, "expenses": 8900.00 }
  ]
}
```

**GET /api/dashboard/categories**

Returns Revenue vs Expense breakdown — total amount, record count, and percentage for each category.

**Authentication required:** Yes

**Note:** The dataset contains exactly 2 categories: `"Revenue"` and `"Expense"`.

**Success 200:**

```json
}
```

item.name: Transactions
item.description:
CRUD and export endpoints for transaction records.

All endpoints require Bearer `{{authToken}}`.

**Dataset facts:**
- 300 total records
- `amount` is always positive; direction is determined by `category`
- `category` values: `Revenue`, `Expense`
- `status` values: `Paid`, `Pending`
- `user_id` values: `user_001`, `user_002`, `user_003`, `user_004`
- Date range: January 2024 – December 2024

query.description: Sort field: date | amount | category | status | user_id | id

request.description:
**GET /api/transactions**

Returns a paginated list of transactions. Supports search, filtering, sorting, and pagination via query parameters.

**Authentication required:** Yes

**All query parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `search` | string | — | Searches user_id, category, status, numeric id, amount, and date (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `dateFrom` | ISO date | — | Start of date range (inclusive) |
| `dateTo` | ISO date | — | End of date range (inclusive, set to end of day) |
| `amountMin` | number | — | Minimum transaction amount |
| `amountMax` | number | — | Maximum transaction amount |
| `category` | Revenue\|Expense | — | Filter by category |
| `status` | Paid\|Pending | — | Filter by status |
| `user_id` | string | — | Filter by user: user_001–user_004 |
| `sortField` | string | date | date, amount, category, status, user_id, id |
| `sortDir` | asc\|desc | desc | Sort direction |
| `page` | integer | 1 | Page number (1-based) |
| `limit` | integer | 10 | Records per page (max 100) |

**Success 200:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": [ { "_id": "...", "id": 247, "date": "...", "amount": 2700, ... } ],
  "pagination": { "page": 1, "limit": 10, "total": 300, "totalPages": 30 }
}
```

exec: // Save first transaction _id for use in 'Get Transaction by ID'

query.description: Text search across user_id, category, status, numeric id, amount, and date

request.description:
**GET /api/transactions?search=Revenue**

Real-time search across transaction fields. The `search` parameter matches against:
- `user_id` (regex, case-insensitive)
- `category` (regex, case-insensitive)
- `status` (regex, case-insensitive)
- `id` (exact numeric match)
- `amount` (exact numeric match)
- `date` (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. search `"2024-01"` matches all January 2024 records)

**Try these search values:**
- `"Revenue"` — all revenue transactions
- `"Paid"` — all paid transactions
- `"user_001"` — transactions for user_001
- `"2024-06"` — all June 2024 transactions
- `"3200"` — transactions with amount 3200

**GET /api/transactions?category=Expense**

Filters transactions to a specific category.

**Allowed values:** `Revenue`, `Expense`

**GET /api/transactions?status=Pending**

Filters transactions by status.

**Allowed values:** `Paid`, `Pending`

query.description: End date (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive (set to end of day)

request.description:
**GET /api/transactions?dateFrom=2024-01-01&dateTo=2024-03-31**

Filters transactions to a date range. `dateTo` is automatically extended to 23:59:59 of that day so the full day is included.

**GET /api/transactions?amountMin=1000&amountMax=3000**

Filters transactions where `amount` is between `amountMin` and `amountMax` (both inclusive).

**Note:** Amounts in the dataset are always positive (150–5000). The display sign (+ / −) is derived from `category` on the frontend.

query.description: user_001 (Alex Morgan) | user_002 (Jamie Chen) | user_003 (Riley Johnson) | user_004 (Sam Williams)

request.description:
**GET /api/transactions?user_id=user_001**

Filters transactions to a specific user.

**User ID to display name mapping:**
- `user_001` → Alex Morgan
- `user_002` → Jamie Chen
- `user_003` → Riley Johnson
- `user_004` → Sam Williams

**GET /api/transactions (combined filters)**

Demonstrates combining multiple filter parameters in a single request:
- category = Revenue
- status = Paid
- date range = Jun–Dec 2024
- amount ≥ 1500
- sorted by amount descending

All filter parameters are combined with AND logic in the MongoDB query.

query.description: Allowed: date | amount | category | status | user_id | id

request.description:
**GET /api/transactions?sortField=amount&sortDir=asc**

Sorts transactions by amount ascending (smallest first).

**Sortable fields:** `date`, `amount`, `category`, `status`, `user_id`, `id`
**Sort directions:** `asc`, `desc`

**GET /api/transactions?page=2&limit=25**

Demonstrates server-side pagination. Returns records 26–50.

The response includes a `pagination` object:
```json
{ "page": 2, "limit": 25, "total": 300, "totalPages": 12 }
```

**GET /api/transactions/:id**

Returns a single transaction by its MongoDB ObjectId.

**Authentication required:** Yes

**URL parameter:**
- `:id` — MongoDB ObjectId (24-char hex string). Use `{{sampleTransactionId}}` which is auto-populated by the *Get All Transactions* test script, or replace with a real `_id` from the database.

**Success 200:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "_id": "60f7...",
    "id": 42,
    "date": "2024-02-21T11:43:30.000Z",
    "amount": 850.00,
    "category": "Expense",
    "status": "Pending",
    "user_id": "user_002",
    "user_profile": "https://thispersondoesnotexist.com/",
    "userName": "Jamie Chen"
  }
}
```

**Error 404:**
```json
{ "success": false, "error": { "code": "NOT_FOUND", "message": "Transaction not found" } }
```

**POST /api/transactions/export**

Generates and returns a CSV file for all transactions (no filters). The browser receives the file as an attachment download.

**Authentication required:** Yes

**Request body:**
- `fields` (string[], required) — columns to include. Allowed values: `id`, `date`, `amount`, `category`, `status`, `userName`, `user_id`, `user_profile`
- `filters` (object, optional) — same filter params as GET /api/transactions. Empty object `{}` = export all 300 records.

**Response:**
```
Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="transactions_export_2024-01-01T00-00-00.csv"

ID,Date,Amount,Category,Status,User Name,User ID,User Profile URL
1,2024-01-15T08:34:12.000Z,1500,Revenue,Paid,Alex Morgan,user_001,https://...
...
```

**Error 400** (no fields selected):
```json
{ "success": false, "error": { "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "At least one field must be selected for export" } }
```

**Note:** In Postman, click **Send and Download** to save the CSV file to disk.

**POST /api/transactions/export (with filters)**

Exports only Revenue + Paid transactions with a subset of columns.

Demonstrates that the `filters` body param respects all the same filter logic as GET /api/transactions (category, status, date range, amount range, user_id, search).

**Note:** Use **Send and Download** in Postman to save the file.

**POST /api/transactions/export (minimal columns + date filter)**

Exports only 4 columns for H1 2024 transactions. Demonstrates configurable column selection.

The `fields` array drives which columns appear in the CSV. Column order matches the array order. Human-readable headers are used (e.g. `amount` → `Amount`).
